notes.decision: Tentatively rendered 'judiciousness' as a quality paired with righteousness in a judicial context. The Lyc. ⲝ corresponds to ϫ; the root may be ϫⲡⲓⲟ ('rebuke, accuse') giving 'judicious-rebuke, censorial uprightness,' or ϫⲱⲡⲉ in another sense. Confidence low; flagged for terminology review.

Translated 'wicked' (qualitative adjective). The form recurs in line 24 modifying 'his other [associates]' where a negative-moral sense fits. Etymology unclear — possibly a Lyc. reflex of a defilement-root. Confidence low. Alternative reading 'concerning her/it' (= ⲉⲧⲃⲏⲏⲧⲥ̄) is grammatically possible but contextually weak.

Tentatively 'destroying them' as a verb of violent action paired with ⲍⲁⲧⲃⲟⲩ 'killing them.' The form is unclear — possibly Lyc. for ϩⲏⲧ-ⲟⲩ ('cast/throw them down') or a related destruction-verb. Flagged for review.
Translated 'obey' as Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'listen, hear, obey.' The negation ⲁⲛ in 'those who do not obey' fits the disciplinary context of the preceding judicial sequence.
Per accumulated vocabulary, ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ = 'intent/purpose of heart.' Here applied to the servants of the judge: 'they do the intent (= will) of their lord.'

Tentatively 'his other associates/companions' — ⲇⲁⲙ uncertain, possibly a noun for confederate/cohort, or possibly an abbreviation for a power-class (δαίμων > 'demons,' or δύναμις > 'powers'). The compound on line 26, ⲛ̄ⲇⲁⲙⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'companions of Sin,' supports a 'companion/associate' reading.

Translated 'companions of Sin.' The construction ⲛ̄-ⲇⲁⲙ-ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ where ⲇⲁⲙ functions as 'fellow, associate' yields 'fellow-sinners, accomplices in sin' — the archons who collaborated with the King of Darkness in the assault on the First Man. Capitalized 'Sin' per terminology guide for cosmic principle.

ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲟⲩⲁ-ϩⲏⲧ = 'state of single-heartedness' = 'single-mindedness, audacity, defiance.' Paired here antithetically with ⲡⲉϩⲑⲃ̄ⲓ̈ⲟ 'his abasement': the judge measures each one according to (1) the boldness of his transgression and (2) the resulting humiliation. Rendered 'single-mindedness' to preserve the etymological one-heartedness.

Tentatively 'he scourged/afflicted them backward.' ⲉϣⲧ likely from a root meaning 'afflict, torment, scourge'; ⲥⲁⲭⲱⲩ likely Lyc. ⲥⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'behind, backward.' Possibly the Manichaean image of binding the archons facing-away from the realm of light.
